actors.name: Apple
actors.role: sells the devices through which most consumers meet AI, and the services layer on top of them

triad.information: owns the customer relationship and the usage data of its device base
triad.execution: designs hardware and software together and has others build and supply them at scale
triad.environment: US consumer and tariff policy: a tariff refund added about a point to its Q4 gross margin

actors.advantage: An installed base locked into one ecosystem (switching costs) and a brand that carries a premium price; Services then earns on that base without the cost of building the hardware again. Rivals can make a phone but not copy the base. It is the largest company on the scoreboard.
actors.desire: to keep the device and Services flywheel growing: its CEO calls the year its best fiscal year ever
actors.fear: that the AI interface moves to someone else's model or device and the base stops being the gate; and that tariffs return

actors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
actors.role: a holding company that turns insurance float and cash flow into ownership of other firms; the economy's patient buyer

triad.information: decades of capital-allocation judgement that now passes from Buffett to Abel
triad.execution: buys whole businesses and leaves operators alone; keeps a very large cash buffer
triad.environment: its cash earns interest at 3.75 to 4.00 percent funds-rate levels while it waits

actors.advantage: Cheap, sticky capital (insurance float) plus the ability to wait. Its advantage is the option to buy when others must sell. A cash pile of $365.5 billion is a weapon in a crisis and a drag in a boom; in 2026 the new CEO began to spend it.
actors.desire: to buy great businesses at fair prices when fear makes them cheap
actors.fear: a permanent loss of capital and a market in which nothing is cheap enough to buy

actors.name: JPMorgan Chase
actors.role: the largest US bank; the plumbing through which AI-era capital raising and trading passes

triad.information: sees payments, lending and trading flows across the economy
triad.execution: runs consumer, investment-banking and markets businesses at scale
triad.environment: gains when rates are high and capital markets are busy

actors.advantage: Balance-sheet scale and the deposit base lower its cost of funds; being the dealer in the biggest capital raisings gives it fees from the AI financing boom. A bank's rivals are regulation and its own credit losses more than other banks.
actors.desire: to be the bank every large capital raising and payment flows through
actors.fear: a credit event in the loans and bonds that fund the AI build, and rules that cap its balance sheet

actors.name: Eli Lilly
actors.role: the leader of the GLP-1 obesity and diabetes drug wave, now the thirteenth largest company in the world

triad.information: clinical data and the patents behind tirzepatide
triad.execution: manufactures injectables at huge volume and launched Zepbound fast
triad.environment: a US market where a patented drug earns a premium and an obesity epidemic supplies demand

actors.advantage: A patented molecule that works better than the first generation, protected for years, made at a scale rivals struggle to match; volume rose while price fell. Revenue rose 39% in Q3 2026 and guidance rose to $91-$92 billion. The advantage is a cornered resource (the patent) turned into process power (supply).
actors.desire: to make GLP-1 the default treatment for obesity and widen into new indications
actors.fear: price cuts from payers and governments, a rival with a better pill, and patent expiry

actors.name: Novo Nordisk
actors.role: the first mover in GLP-1 for obesity (Wegovy), now defending against Lilly

triad.information: first clinical evidence for semaglutide in obesity
triad.execution: scaled supply, then right-sized its factory network after a slowdown
triad.environment: a market whose growth drew a stronger rival

actors.advantage: It created the category and still claims more than half of branded new patient starts in the US, and launched a Wegovy pill. But it expects 2026 adjusted sales growth of only -2% to +2%, while Lilly grows 39%: a first mover whose advantage was copied faster than it could be protected.
actors.desire: to keep leadership in obesity care with the Wegovy pill and new launches
actors.fear: losing the lead to Lilly, and price pressure; it took impairment charges in Q3 2026

actors.name: Walmart
actors.role: the largest physical retail distribution network, growing a digital and advertising business on top of it

triad.information: sees what a very large share of US households buy, which feeds its ad business
triad.execution: supply chain and low prices at scale

actors.advantage: Purchasing and logistics scale allow the lowest prices; the store network turns into fast delivery that online rivals cannot copy cheaply; advertising on its own data (up 38% in Q2 FY27) earns a margin that groceries cannot. It stands as the consumer end of the global supply chain.
actors.desire: to be the cheapest and the fastest and to add high-margin advertising and membership
actors.fear: consumers trading down or away, and tariffs on imported goods

actors.name: Visa
actors.role: the rail on which card payments run: a toll on consumption

triad.information: sees transaction data across the world
triad.execution: runs an authorisation network at high uptime
triad.environment: grows with nominal spending and cross-border travel, so inflation helps it

actors.advantage: A two-sided network: more cards make merchants accept Visa, more merchants make cards worth carrying (network economies). It takes a small fee on every payment and carries little capital, so its margins are very high. It is a choke point for consumption, not for AI.
actors.desire: to be the default rail for new forms of payment
actors.fear: regulation of card fees, and a rival rail (account-to-account, stablecoins)

actors.name: Mastercard
actors.role: the other card rail
actors.advantage: The twin of Visa in a duopoly; it shares the same network economics.

actors.name: Saudi Aramco
actors.role: the world's largest oil producer by value; the Gulf's cash machine

triad.information: knows its reservoirs and the oil market better than anyone
triad.execution: runs production, refining and chemicals at huge scale
triad.environment: sits inside the Gulf: the geology is its advantage and the Strait of Hormuz is its exposure

actors.advantage: Ownership of low-cost reserves, a state that backs it, and a downstream arm that earns when refining margins widen. In Q3 2026 its adjusted net income rose to $31.2 billion and downstream earnings jumped 234% while the Iran war pushed oil up; it pays a $21.9 billion quarterly base dividend to its shareholders.
actors.desire: to keep the dividend and fund diversification into refining and chemicals
actors.fear: attacks on its facilities and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and demand destruction if prices stay high

actors.name: Exxon Mobil
actors.role: the largest Western oil major
actors.advantage: A scoreboard entry: integrated scale in oil and gas, benefiting from the 2026 oil shock; see the notes.

actors.name: Johnson & Johnson
actors.role: a diversified healthcare group
actors.advantage: A scoreboard entry: diversified pharma and devices.

actors.name: AbbVie
actors.role: a large immunology and neuroscience drug maker
actors.advantage: A scoreboard entry: patented biologics.

actors.name: Tesla
actors.role: electric-car maker repositioning as an AI and robotics company

triad.information: fleet data from millions of cars
triad.environment: US policy on credits and tariffs; competes against subsidised Chinese makers

actors.advantage: A first-mover in electric cars with in-house manufacturing, but in 2026 it has been overtaken in battery-electric volume by BYD (Q3: 486,532 vs 762,478) and its operating margin fell to 2.6%. It is spending (capex $4.73 billion in Q3, R&D up sharply) on robotaxis and robots: a bet that its advantage moves from cars to autonomy and data. The market still values it at $1.415 trillion, tenth in the world.
actors.desire: to make autonomy and robots the next business, funded by the cars
actors.fear: BYD's cost lead in cars and failing to make robotaxis pay before the cars' margin runs out

actors.name: BYD
actors.role: China's battery-and-car maker; the world's largest battery-electric seller by units

triad.execution: builds its own batteries, chips and cars, which lets it cut cost fast
triad.environment: China's industrial policy, the largest home market and its supply of batteries

actors.advantage: A vertically integrated maker with a cost advantage; it sold 762,478 passenger BEVs in Q3 2026, widening its lead over Tesla to about 276,000. Its position rests on the Chinese supply chain, not on a single technology.
actors.desire: to lead the world in electric vehicles
actors.fear: trade barriers abroad and price wars at home

actors.name: SpaceX
actors.role: a rocket maker, satellite network and AI lab now listed as the seventh largest company; its IPO priced at $135 a share

triad.environment: capital markets let it list at a value above $2 trillion on day one, and US government contracts

actors.advantage: A reusable launch system gives the lowest cost to orbit; that cost lets it build a satellite network, and the listing gives it capital to follow into AI. The market values it at $1.823 trillion. Tesla holds a stake in it.
actors.desire: to extend the launch advantage into a space-and-AI conglomerate
actors.fear: an IPO valuation that assumes growth it cannot deliver, and loss of government favour

actors.name: Tencent
actors.role: China's largest social, games and payment platform; spending heavily on AI compute

triad.information: the data of a very large number of WeChat users
triad.execution: ships AI features into an app everyone already uses
triad.environment: China's regulation and export controls on chips

actors.advantage: WeChat's network gives it distribution for any AI product; Q2 2026 revenue rose 11% (US$30.36 billion) while it stepped up compute purchases and profit rose only 0.7%. Its fear is the chip supply.
actors.desire: to convert usage of its apps and models into revenue, in its own words
actors.fear: not being able to buy enough compute, and a slowdown in advertising

actors.name: Federal Reserve
actors.role: sets the price of money for every company
actors.advantage: Not a firm: it sets the environment. On 28 October 2026 it held at 3-3/4 to 4 percent by 10-2 with two members preferring a rise; inflation remains elevated.

actors.name: Public markets
actors.role: the pool of capital that values and funds the largest firms
actors.advantage: Concentrated: the ten largest S&P 500 members are 39.1% of its value and the largest alone is 8.4%; a loss of faith in the top names is a loss of faith in the index.
actors.fear: a fall in the AI leaders

actors.name: Venture capital
actors.role: the openness engine: it pays for new firms to try to beat the old ones
actors.advantage: US venture investment reached $515.8 billion through Q3 2026, a record; AI took 82.7% of it, so the risk-taking system is now one bet.
actors.fear: a failed exit window: exits stay limited

flashpoints.title: GLP-1: Lilly passes Novo
flashpoints.advantage: a patented drug that works better, made at volume
flashpoints.mechanism: Novo made the market; Lilly's tirzepatide took the growth by working better and scaling faster, and grew volume faster than rivals.
flashpoints.outcome: Lilly Q3 revenue $24.40 billion, +39%; Novo guides 2026 adjusted sales to -2% to +2%; Lilly's market cap $1.206 trillion (rank 13).

flashpoints.title: BYD out-builds Tesla
flashpoints.mechanism: BYD makes its own batteries and cars at a cost Tesla cannot match; Tesla answers by moving its story to autonomy and robots.
flashpoints.outcome: Q3 2026 deliveries: BYD 762,478 passenger BEVs, Tesla 486,532; Tesla's operating margin 2.6%; Tesla still valued at $1.415 trillion.

flashpoints.title: Apple and the tariff refunds
flashpoints.advantage: scale and brand that absorb a trade shock
flashpoints.mechanism: Apple's scale let it take the tariff cost; when the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs the refunds returned about a point of gross margin.
flashpoints.outcome: Gross margin 47.9% in fiscal Q4 2026; projected refunds up to $175 billion across firms.

flashpoints.title: SpaceX lists and passes Tesla
flashpoints.advantage: capital: the market pays for a launch monopoly plus AI
flashpoints.mechanism: A company with the lowest cost to orbit used the public market to raise at a valuation above $2 trillion; it now ranks seventh and Tesla tenth.
flashpoints.outcome: IPO at $135, closed near $161 on day one; scoreboard market cap $1.823 trillion against Tesla's $1.415 trillion.

flashpoints.title: The Iran war lifts the oil majors
flashpoints.advantage: low-cost reserves, and a position at the sea lane
flashpoints.mechanism: War in the Gulf disrupted flows through Hormuz and lifted oil; Aramco's refining margins widened, but its facilities were attacked.
flashpoints.outcome: Aramco Q3 adjusted net income $31.2 billion (from $28.6 billion); EIA expects Brent about $98 in 2026.

flashpoints.title: Berkshire starts spending the cash
flashpoints.advantage: the patience that only cheap, sticky capital allows
flashpoints.mechanism: Berkshire kept a cash mountain while prices were high; under its new CEO it began deploying it.
flashpoints.outcome: Cash fell 8.0% to $365.5 billion from a record $397.4 billion.

flashpoints.title: Rates against the AI build-out
flashpoints.advantage: control of the cost of capital
flashpoints.mechanism: Inflation remains elevated and two members wanted a rise; the price of money decides whether $725 billion of annual capex is paid for by cash flow or by debt.
flashpoints.outcome: Funds-rate range held at 3-3/4 to 4 percent by a 10-2 vote.

notes: Not verified and left out of the numbers: Walmart's Q2 FY27 total revenue ($187.9 billion by secondary press; its release page is a slide script and Chain Store Age refused the script) and Walmart's operating income; Lilly's own 8-K and press release (SEC and investor.lilly.com returned 403), so Lilly's figures come from Zacks; Novo's adjusted operating profit; Apple's iPhone and Services split (sources disagree: 57.6 vs 54.3 billion); JPMorgan's revenue; Berkshire's Q3 2026 results (nothing found yet, so the latest cash figure is 30 June 2026); SpaceX's IPO proceeds (a reported $75 billion) and its revenue; Tesla's 2026 capex guidance (sources disagree: more than $25 billion vs $20 billion); the current US effective tariff rate and the status of the Section 122 tariff (sources conflict); Aramco's average realised crude price ($95.2 a barrel by secondary press); Tencent's Q2 capex (RMB 52.8 billion by press). Founding years in the actor records come from general knowledge and are not gated. Market caps are one snapshot of one aggregator (companiesmarketcap.com, 7 November 2026, a total of $146.443 trillion across 11,396 companies) and move daily; CompaniesMarketCap lists Samsung, SK Hynix and others by local listing. The 'AI contributes about one-third of 2026 US growth' claim is ING's judgement, quoted in a fact note; the 50.2% figure is a gross measure without subtracting imports, and Goldman Sachs argues the net effect is much smaller.
openQuestions: Is the 2026 US growth supported by AI capex net of imports, or is the 50.2% gross figure mostly imported hardware?
Does the Fed's next move (two members wanted a hike) fall before or after the hyperscalers have to finance the next leg of capex with debt?
Does Lilly's growth hold once payers and governments push on GLP-1 prices?
What is the current effective US tariff rate after the Section 122 surcharge ended, and who now bears it?
How much of Berkshire's remaining cash will Abel deploy before the next downturn, and into what?
Which non-AI leaders (Walmart, Visa, JPMorgan) are exposed to an AI-capex pullback through consumers and credit rather than directly?
